name: store_slots_and_copy_block
description: Writes three successive addresses into one fixed memory slot, calling an unnamed routine after each write. It then copies a block of words from the routine's own code area to a fixed destination address.

name: invoke_single_unnamed_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The listed facts show an eight-instruction routine that one unnamed routine calls and that calls one unnamed routine.

name: copy_counted_word_block
description: Copies a counted block of words from one pointer to another, with the count held in a data register. The facts also list the colour register as touched, and two unnamed routines call it.

name: write_fat_marker_by_flag
description: Writes one of two four-character text markers, FAT0 or FAT1, into a memory location, choosing FAT1 when a flag bit of a global value is set. The facts list the vertical position status register as touched, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: detect_refresh_rate_hz
description: Resets the CIA-A and CIA-B port and timer registers, then reads a counter from two timer bytes and returns 50 or 60 depending on whether it is below a threshold. It also writes the text marker MF50 or MF60 into a memory structure.

name: wait_until_status_byte_clear
description: Loops reading a status byte at a fixed offset from a base register until its top bit is clear, then returns minus one. A self-comparison in the loop can return zero but never does, so it has no effect on the result.

name: build_ram_tag_records
description: Clears a 188-byte area, writes the text tags RAMC and RAMF into it, and stores two values returned by an unnamed routine. It then loops over a fixed count, storing RAMP-tagged records for addresses below a limit and otherwise saving the value into fields.

name: walk_list_from_base_field
description: Loads a list head from a field of the base-register structure, then walks the linked list. It stops at a null link or at the first node whose stored word has the bit selected by a counter register set, and it is called by one unnamed routine.

name: walk_list_until_bit_set
description: Walks a linked list starting from the pointer passed in an address register, stopping at a null link or at the first node whose stored word has the bit selected by a counter register set. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: save_fpu_state_on_flag
description: When a global flag byte is clear, it writes a combined control word into a structure field and returns. When the flag is set, it saves the floating-point state frame and stores a pointer into a fixed vector slot, while the decompiler marks the tail as bad instruction data, so that tail is unreliable.

name: copy_long_and_store_tag
description: Copies one 32-bit value from a source address to a destination address, then writes a combined word, built from a data register and a fixed constant, into a field of a structure. The routine is called by two unnamed routines.

name: store_constant_in_global
description: Stores a single constant into a global variable and returns. The facts also list the interrupt enable register as touched, which the pseudo-code does not show directly.

name: delegate_to_unnamed_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The listed facts show a four-instruction entry routine that is reached from outside the normal code flow and calls one unnamed routine.

name: configure_chipset_registers_and_calls
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so only the listed facts are known. The routine touches the two CIA port registers, the colour register, the DMA and interrupt control registers and the custom chip base, and calls seven unnamed routines; one tiny stub routine calls it.

name: poll_routine_until_zero
description: Calls an unnamed routine once, and if the zero flag is clear, repeats that call while a short value in a data register is nonzero, then returns zero. The routine was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data rather than code.

name: repeat_call_until_result_one
description: Calls an unnamed routine to obtain a value, then repeatedly calls it again with that value, storing the upper half of each 64-bit result through a pointer until the lower half equals one. It then calls the same routine once more and returns zero.

name: repeat_call_until_result_one
description: Has the same code as the previous routine and was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data rather than code. It repeatedly calls one unnamed routine, storing the upper half of each 64-bit result through a pointer until the lower half equals one.

name: read_header_fields_and_count
description: Calls an unnamed routine in a loop until a status value is zero, then reads three values into fields of a structure and clears two other fields. It then calls the same routine a number of times set by the first value, counting the calls in a field.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The decoded pseudo-code is only a return, so the routine does nothing in the code shown. The listed facts record one unnamed call that the pseudo-code does not show.

name: poll_routine_until_zero
description: Calls an unnamed routine once, and if the zero flag is clear, repeats that call while a short value in a data register is nonzero, then returns zero. The facts list three unnamed callers and four unnamed callees, while the pseudo-code shows only the one repeated call.

name: accumulate_table_value_into_pointers
description: While an unnamed routine returns a nonzero value, it takes an index from another unnamed routine, looks up a value in a table within the structure, and adds that value into memory at each offset produced by repeated calls until the low word returned equals one. The routine returns zero, and the facts list a callee that just returns zero.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The decompiled pseudo-code is only a return, although the facts list 26 instructions, two unnamed callers and two unnamed callees, so the body is not recoverable from the pseudo-code. Nothing beyond those listed facts is known about it.

name: store_result_select_entry
description: Calls one unnamed routine and stores its result in a structure field, then sets a flag byte to 255. It returns a 32-bit entry from a table in the structure, chosen by a word index field.

name: return_table_entry_by_index
description: Returns a 32-bit entry from a table in the structure, selected by a word index field. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: store_table_entry_from_result
description: Calls one unnamed routine and stores its result in a structure field with the top two bits cleared, choosing between two unnamed routines by the top bits of a value. The result plus 32 is written into a table entry, and the pseudo-code shows an endless loop when the result is zero; the routine also references the text tags RAMC, RAMF and RAMP and touches the colour register.

name: clear_flag_and_increment_counter
description: If a flag byte in the structure is nonzero, it clears the flag and increments a short counter field; otherwise it does nothing. The facts list one unnamed caller.

name: init_global_pointer_fields
description: Stores the address of a global variable into a structure pointer slot, writes a data register value and a zero into two structure fields, then calls one unnamed routine. The facts list one unnamed caller.

name: read_next_long_and_advance
description: Reads a 32-bit value through a pointer stored in the structure, then advances that pointer by one long and reduces a byte-count field by four. When the count field is zero it first calls one unnamed routine, and the value is returned as a 64-bit result with a data register.

name: forward_routine_result_pair
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns the two data registers it leaves as a 64-bit result. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: decompress_bit_stream_block
description: Unpacks a compressed block by reading bits from a stream: each step either copies earlier output bytes backwards for a counted length or writes literal bytes assembled from bit fields. It stops when the output pointer reaches its limit and returns a value derived from two header words.

name: rotate_right_extend_long
description: Returns a 32-bit word read from memory, shifted right one bit, with the extend-flag bit placed at the top and the top bit forced set. It is a rotate-through-extend step, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: rotate_bits_through_extend
description: Rotates a 32-bit register right one bit at a time, feeding in the extend bit and reloading from a memory word whenever the register empties, for a count taken from a data register. Three unnamed routines call it and it calls two.

name: init_bitstream_state_fields
description: Sets a 16-bit field to a fixed constant, copies a 32-bit value into another field, and adds 11 to a short field. It then calls one unnamed routine, and two unnamed routines call it.

name: sum_tagged_ram_records
description: Scans 64 entries of a fixed low-memory table and, for each entry whose tag matches the text RAM followed by M, adds the 32-bit value stored eight bytes after the tag to a running total, which it returns. The routine was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data rather than code.

name: find_table_entry_by_key
description: Searches a 64-entry table in a fixed low-memory area for a 32-bit key equal to a data register value. When it finds a match it returns the two longs stored with that entry as a 64-bit result, and otherwise it returns a fallback value passed in another data register.

name: clear_global_memory_and_init
description: Zeroes about 19 kilobytes of global memory word by word, then runs a sequence of calls to unnamed routines. It stores a fixed limit into a memory field and calls one more routine when a value returned by a call exceeds that limit.

name: accumulate_contiguous_ram_records
description: Walks a chain of records tagged RAMP while each record's start address continues from the previous one, adding their sizes into a running total. It then stores the accumulated size into a field and clears a second field; the loop ends at the first record that lacks the tag or does not continue the sequence.

name: append_ram_split_record
description: Finds the first empty slot in a table of four-long records and writes a RAMD tag record there. The record stores a fixed boundary of 512 kilobytes and the remainder of a data register after subtracting that boundary.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Does nothing except call one unnamed routine and return. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: dispatch_on_ram_tag
description: Dispatches on a tag argument. For the RAMC tag it calls one unnamed routine and, when the first argument was zero, follows it with a call that passes the RAMD tag; for any other tag it makes a single call, and the pseudo-code shows that call as its only effect.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Does nothing except call one unnamed routine and return. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: set_flag_around_routine_call
description: Sets a byte at a fixed memory address to 255, calls one unnamed routine, then clears that byte to zero. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: forward_ram_tag_unless_flagged
description: Passes a tag argument on to one unnamed routine. When the tag is RAMC and a flag byte in the structure is clear, it instead calls an unnamed routine without the argument and returns without forwarding.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Does nothing except call one unnamed routine and return. The facts show four unnamed callers.

name: allocate_block_from_pool
description: Allocates a block from a pool whose remaining size is held in a word, rounding the requested size up to a multiple of four and adding a four-byte header. It reduces the pool size, stores the new block's address and clears its first long, and returns zero when the second argument is zero or the pool is too small.

name: clear_longs_when_flag_clear
description: If a flag byte in the structure is zero, it writes zero into consecutive longs from a pointer, covering the requested byte count divided by four. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: walk_list_to_last_node
description: Follows a chain of pointers, where each node's first long points to the next node, until it reaches a node whose link is null, then returns the incoming low byte unchanged. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: advance_to_list_tail
description: Follows a chain of pointers until it reaches a node whose first long is null, then returns with no result. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Does nothing except call one unnamed routine and return. The facts show one unnamed caller and one unnamed callee.

name: return_routine_result_once
description: Calls one unnamed routine once and returns its result. The nested checks depend on a flag that the pseudo-code never sets, so their branches are never taken.

name: return_pair_after_hardware_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns the two data registers unchanged as a 64-bit result. The facts list the CIA port registers and the custom chip base as touched, though the pseudo-code shows only the call.

name: return_pair_after_hardware_call
description: Has the same code as the previous routine and returns the two data registers unchanged after one call to an unnamed routine. The facts list the CIA port registers and the custom chip base as touched, though the pseudo-code shows only the call.

name: step_counter_modulo_eleven
description: Stores two data registers into a structure, divides a 16-bit count by eleven and stores the quotient and remainder in fields. It then loops stepping a byte field through the values zero to ten, carrying into a counter field, and calls unnamed routines at each step until a termination condition holds; the facts list five unnamed callees.

name: pulse_control_register_bit
description: Writes a sequence of bit operations to a control byte at a fixed offset from a base register: it sets the top bit, clears bit one and sets the high bits, then clears and sets a bit chosen by a counter register. It calls one unnamed routine and returns the incoming word unchanged.

name: wait_while_status_bit_set
description: Calls two unnamed routines, then keeps calling a third while a status byte has a particular bit set. The facts list one unnamed caller.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: Moves a stored position word one step at a time toward a target word, calling an unnamed routine at each step with the calls depending on parity. It then copies the target into the position, writes two constant bytes to fixed offsets, and waits until a status bit is set.

name: set_control_bit_one
description: Sets bit one of a byte at a fixed offset from a base register. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: clear_control_bit_one
description: Clears bit one of a byte at a fixed offset from a base register. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: poll_status_bit_with_limit
description: Clears the top bit of a control byte and then a counter-selected bit, then polls a status byte through an unnamed routine up to fifteen times, returning as soon as one bit is clear. It returns the incoming word, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: write_bytes_and_wait_ready
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then writes the low and high bytes of a 16-bit argument to two fixed offsets from a base register. It then waits until a ready bit at another offset is set; eight unnamed routines call it.

name: update_control_bytes_pair
description: Keeps the top two bits of one control byte and adds eight to them, then writes 127 to a second control byte at a fixed offset from a base register. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: write_constants_then_wait_ready
description: Calls two unnamed routines, writes two constant bytes to fixed offsets from a base register, then waits until a ready bit at a third offset is set. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: clear_set_bit_then_wait
description: Clears bit zero of a control byte, calls an unnamed routine, sets bit zero again and calls another routine. It then writes 100 and 8 to two fixed offsets and waits until a ready bit is set; three unnamed routines call it.

name: set_control_bit_group_call
description: Sets a group of bits in a control byte, bits three to six, then calls one unnamed routine and returns the incoming word unchanged. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: start_sync_word_transfer
description: Writes a fixed sync word into a buffer and into several hardware registers, then polls a status bit through an unnamed routine up to fifteen times. It returns zero when the bit is seen and a fixed negative error value otherwise.

name: decode_sector_after_sync
description: Scans a buffer for the sync word and checks a decoded byte against a stored value; when they match it decodes data into a destination, either byte by byte or as a block of 128 longs covering 512 bytes. It advances the stored destination pointer and returns zero on success, or a fixed negative error value after the buffer scans fail.

name: merge_masked_words_doubled
description: Combines two memory words under a mask: bits from the first word are kept where the mask is set, and bits from the second word are doubled before being merged in. It returns the combined value, and three unnamed routines call it.

name: invoke_entry_stub_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The listed facts show a two-instruction routine that is reached from outside the static code flow and is called by one unnamed routine.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The decoded pseudo-code only tests a flag and returns, with no effect. The listed facts show one call to an empty routine that returns immediately.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The routine is a single return instruction, so it does nothing. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The routine is a single return instruction, so it does nothing. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The routine is a single return instruction, so it does nothing. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: call_routines_referencing_intro_text
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the calls cannot be read. The listed facts show text references to OSEmu.400 and intro.code, a call to a two-instruction routine that loads a constant into a data register, and six unnamed callees.

name: patch_jump_slots_and_call
description: Writes no-operation instruction pairs and absolute jump instructions into fixed code locations, with each jump pointing to an unnamed routine, then calls four unnamed routines. It returns the two data registers unchanged, and the facts list five small routines that each load constants into a data register.

name: patch_code_slots_then_call
description: Writes no-operation instruction pairs and absolute jump instructions into six fixed code locations, then calls four unnamed routines. It returns the two data registers unchanged, and the facts list four small routines that each load constants into a data register.

name: patch_code_slots_with_jumps
description: Writes a constant word pair into one memory location, then writes no-operation pairs, a load-small-constant instruction and absolute jump instructions into fixed code locations. It then calls three unnamed routines and returns the two data registers unchanged.

name: patch_two_jump_slots
description: Writes no-operation pairs and two absolute jump instructions into fixed code locations, each jump pointing to an unnamed routine, then calls three unnamed routines. It returns the 64-bit result with a fixed constant ORed into its high bits; this routine has the same code as the next two.

name: patch_two_jump_slots
description: Has the same code as the previous routine: it writes no-operation pairs and two absolute jump instructions into fixed code locations, then calls three unnamed routines and returns a 64-bit result with a fixed constant ORed into its high bits.

name: patch_two_jump_slots
description: Has the same code as the two routines before it: it writes no-operation pairs and two absolute jump instructions into fixed code locations, then calls three unnamed routines and returns a 64-bit result with a fixed constant ORed into its high bits.

name: patch_two_slots_then_call
description: Writes no-operation pairs and two absolute jump instructions into fixed code locations, then calls three unnamed routines. The facts also list garbled text fragments, one small routine that loads a constant into a data register, another that loads a sequence of constants, and six unnamed callees.

name: patch_code_set_global
description: Writes encoded instruction words and no-operation pairs into fixed code locations, then calls three unnamed routines and one more routine. It stores a fixed constant in a global variable and returns the two data registers combined with a fixed high-bit constant.

name: patch_code_then_call_routines
description: Writes the same encoded instruction words and no-operation pairs into fixed code locations, then calls ten unnamed routines and two small constant routines. It stores a fixed constant in a global variable and returns the two data registers unchanged.

name: store_word_result_in_field
description: Calls one unnamed routine and stores its 16-bit result in a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_word_result_in_field
description: Has the same code as the previous routine: it calls one unnamed routine and stores its 16-bit result in a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_word_result_in_field
description: Has the same code as the previous routine, but is decoded as an address taken by a pc-relative push. It calls one unnamed routine and stores its 16-bit result in a structure field.

name: store_word_register_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the 16-bit value left in a data register into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_word_register_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the 16-bit value left in another data register into the same structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 258 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 1,986 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 4,500 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 12,626 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 12,801 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 14,867 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 16,340 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 17,295 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_fixed_word_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then stores the fixed value 17,300 into a structure field. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: wait_while_global_bit_set
description: Busy-waits while bit six of a global flag word stays set, then returns. The facts show it touches the CIA-A port register and the DMA control read register, and twelve unnamed routines call it.

name: write_call_stubs_from_table
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of offsets and, at each offset from a base register, writes a subroutine-call instruction encoding followed by a word argument. Five unnamed routines call it, and the facts list one unnamed callee although the pseudo-code shows no call.

name: write_absolute_call_slots
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of offsets and, at each offset from a base register, writes an absolute subroutine-call instruction followed by a 32-bit argument. Eight unnamed routines call it.

name: write_nop_then_call_slots
description: Was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data. It walks a zero-terminated list of offsets, writing a no-operation followed by an absolute subroutine-call instruction at each one, then a 16-bit argument; the facts list one unnamed callee.

name: write_nop_pairs_at_offsets
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of offsets and writes a pair of no-operation instructions at each offset from a base register. The facts show one unnamed caller and one unnamed callee.

name: call_routines_by_flag_chain
description: Calls through an indirect pointer, then makes between one and four calls to unnamed routines depending on whether a value is zero, chained in nested branches. It references the text names animation.code, final.code, intro.code, score.code and volley.code, and six unnamed routines call it.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated byte strings and returns zero when they are identical, or minus one at the first mismatch. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: decompress_checked_bit_stream
description: Unpacks a compressed block through the bit reader routines, either copying earlier output bytes backwards or writing literal bytes built from bit fields. When the final value differs from a header value it runs a countdown loop that writes into a global variable, and the facts list the colour register as touched.

name: stub_endless_loop
description: The pseudo-code is only an endless loop, with unreachable blocks removed by the decompiler, so nothing beyond the loop is recoverable. The facts list the vertical beam position register as touched and two unnamed callers.

name: compare_result_without_effect
description: Calls one unnamed routine and compares its byte result with a global byte, but both branches return with no effect. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: return_incoming_byte_unchanged
description: Returns the low byte of the incoming data register unchanged and has no other effect. Five unnamed routines call it, and it calls one unnamed routine.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The pseudo-code is only a return. The facts list one unnamed caller and one unnamed callee.

name: entry_point_opens_library
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show this is the program entry point, which calls the system library routines to open and close a library, references the text df0:intro.code and dos.library, and makes one call to an unnamed routine.

name: add_global_loop_or_close
description: Calls a file library routine and, when the result is zero, adds 256 to a global variable in a loop of 32,000 passes. Otherwise it calls two more file library routines; the facts list the colour register as touched and one unnamed caller.

name: configure_blitter_and_dma
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show it touches blitter and DMA control registers, the keyboard serial register and a colour register, and calls twenty-one unnamed routines and two tiny routines.

name: write_constant_table_sequence
description: The pseudo-code is a long run of constant writes to global variables and memory fields, interleaved with calls to an unnamed routine. The facts show a single instruction and three tiny callers, so the run may be data that was decoded as code.

name: configure_audio_channel_three
description: Writes a sequence of constants to global variables and fixed memory fields, interleaved with calls to six unnamed routines and a small routine that adds to a register. The facts list the third audio channel registers and the DMA control register as touched.

name: delay_busy_loop_long
description: Busy-waits by counting a 16-bit counter down through 15,000 steps for each of 100 outer passes, then returns. Two tiny routines and one unnamed routine call it.

name: delay_busy_loop_long
description: Has the same code as the previous routine: it busy-waits through 15,000 steps for each of 100 outer passes, then returns. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: delay_busy_loop_short
description: Busy-waits by counting a 16-bit counter down through 400 steps, then returns. The facts show one unnamed caller.

name: adjust_two_counters_below_limit
description: When a frame counter is below 599, it decrements one global word while that word is at least 95 and increments another global word while it is below 46. The facts show one tiny caller.

name: step_frame_counter_and_adjust
description: Advances a frame counter word and, while it lies from 599 up to 988, decrements three global words, calls an unnamed routine and adjusts two more words. It sets a flag once the counter reaches 1,000, and the facts list three unnamed callees and two tiny routines.

name: configure_blitter_three_passes
description: Sets a blitter mask and register values, then runs a three-pass loop that writes blitter pointer registers and calls a fixed low-memory routine on each pass. The facts list the blitter registers and the custom chip base as touched, with one unnamed callee.

name: adjust_counter_pair_limit
description: When a counter word is below 255 and a second word is at most zero, it increments the second word and returns. Otherwise it adjusts the counter pair and subtracts 28 from a fixed memory word; the facts list two unnamed callees.

name: run_blitter_passes_and_step
description: Stores a long at an indexed field, sets blitter registers and then calls a fixed low-memory routine four times with changing pointers. It adjusts two counter words when one is below a limit, and three unnamed routines call it.

name: configure_blitter_four_passes
description: Sets blitter mask and register values, then calls a fixed low-memory routine four times with changing pointers, and adjusts two counter words when one is below a limit. The facts list the blitter registers and the custom chip base as touched, and one tiny routine calls it.

name: start_blitter_passes_and_wait
description: Sets blitter control and pointer values and calls a fixed low-memory routine four times, then waits until a busy flag in a global word clears. The facts list the blitter registers as touched and a blitter wait routine as its callee.

name: configure_blitter_from_rectangle
description: Computes a blitter size from two words of a structure and stores position and offset values, then programs the blitter source, destination and modulo registers over four passes. The facts list the blitter registers as touched, with one tiny and two unnamed callers.

name: interleave_three_tables_into_global
description: Copies three word tables into global memory in an interleaved pattern: for each of sixteen entries it writes a running offset word, starting at 384 and rising by two, followed by a table entry. The facts show one tiny and two unnamed callers.

name: save_custom_registers_then_set
description: Copies five global register values into fields, then writes a routine address and two constants to a global variable. The facts show the audio, DMA, interrupt enable and interrupt request registers as touched, with one tiny and one unnamed caller.

name: restore_saved_custom_registers
description: Writes five saved values back to a global variable, clearing one bit of the first and setting the top bit in four of them. The facts show the audio, DMA and interrupt registers as touched, with one tiny caller.

name: acknowledge_request_flag_bit
description: If bit five of a global word is set, it increments that word, calls an unnamed routine and sets the word to 32; otherwise it sets the word to 4,063 and returns. The facts show the interrupt request registers as touched.

name: set_copper_list_pointers
description: Writes four address pairs into fixed fields, waits until a global word reads minus one, then stores another address and writes a fixed constant. The facts list the copper pointer and jump registers and the vertical position register as touched.

name: swap_copper_list_buffers
description: Toggles a flag to choose between two buffer addresses, waits for a global counter to reach a threshold and then for a handshake value, and writes four address pairs derived from the chosen buffer. It toggles the flag again at the end, and the facts list the vertical position register as touched.

name: select_audio_volume_from_table
description: Scans a table of up to 128 bytes for the first entry greater than the current value, then clears several global words and loads a byte from another table field. The facts list the four audio channel volume registers as touched, and one tiny routine calls it.

name: advance_audio_channel_step
description: Advances a step counter that cycles through five values. On the fifth step it calls three unnamed routines, pauses briefly and updates a global word from a status word; on the other steps it calls up to four routines conditionally. It also advances an index through a 1,024-byte cycle, and the facts list the audio channel pointer registers as touched.

name: apply_channel_command_nibble
description: Decodes the low nibble of a command byte in a structure: codes one and two call an unnamed routine and then decrement or increase a word with limits, code twelve stores a byte, and code fifteen stores a nibble in a global word. When the nibble is zero it looks up a value in a table of global words and stores it.

name: check_pointer_then_return
description: The pseudo-code only compares a pointer with the address of a global variable and returns, so it has no visible effect. The facts list the audio channel registers and the DMA control register as touched, with three unnamed callers, one unnamed callee and two small routines.

name: load_audio_channel_from_table
description: Copies a long from a source buffer into a channel structure, then uses the high nibble of a control byte to select a 30-byte table entry and copies its fields into the channel. The facts list the DMA control register as touched, with one unnamed caller.

name: set_sentinel_then_call_routines
description: Stores a minus-one sentinel into a global long and calls several unnamed routines in sequence, one of which is a jump-table entry that passes control elsewhere. The facts list the text references df0:intro, df0:introp1.cru, df0:trophe.cru and dos.library, and one tiny caller.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: The pseudo-code is only a return. The facts show one unnamed caller and that it was executed in the reference run.

name: add_global_loop_or_close
description: Has the same code as the earlier routine that calls library routines at fixed offsets: it calls a library routine and, when the result is zero, adds 256 to a global variable over 32,000 passes. Otherwise it calls two more library routines, and the facts show one unnamed caller.

name: add_global_loop_passes
description: Adds 256 to a global variable in a loop of 32,000 passes, then returns. The facts show the colour register as touched and one unnamed routine that calls it; the routine was decoded from an unreached gap.

name: inspect_undecoded_routine_body
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a fourteen-instruction routine whose address is taken by an absolute load and which one unnamed routine calls.

name: inspect_undecoded_routine_body
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a one-instruction routine that was executed in the reference run and that one unnamed routine calls.

name: decompress_bit_stream_block
description: Unpacks a compressed block through the bit reader routines, copying earlier output bytes backwards or writing literal bytes built from bit fields. It writes a countdown into a global variable when the final value differs from the header, and was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data.

name: decompress_bit_stream_fragment
description: A fragment of the same bit-stream decoder that enters through a jump label, decoded from an unreached gap so it may be data. It copies earlier output bytes backwards or writes literal bytes, and calls one unnamed routine.

name: decompress_bit_stream_fragment
description: Another fragment of the same bit-stream decoder, decoded from an unreached gap so it may be data. It reads bits and writes literal bytes, and calls two unnamed routines and the bit reader.

name: decompress_bit_stream_fragment
description: A further fragment of the same decoder, reached through a jump label and decoded from an unreached gap. It copies earlier output bytes backwards and calls two unnamed routines and the bit reader.

name: count_global_full_wrap
description: Repeatedly stores a 16-bit counter into a global variable, counting down from minus one through the full 16-bit range until it wraps to zero, then returns. The facts show the colour register as touched and one unnamed caller.

name: decompress_bit_stream_block
description: Unpacks a compressed block of the same kind as the other decoders in this file, with a final countdown into a global variable when the final value differs from the header. The facts show the colour register as touched, one unnamed caller and two unnamed callees.

name: rotate_right_extend_long
description: Returns a 32-bit word read from memory, shifted right one bit, with the top bit forced set. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: rotate_bits_through_extend
description: Rotates a 32-bit register right one bit at a time for a count taken from a data register, reloading from memory whenever the register empties. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: A single return with no effect. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: A single return with no effect. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: A single return with no effect. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: start_animation_code_region
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a raw code region of 149 instructions starting at the beginning of the file, which touches the audio channel volume registers, an audio length register, the fire button port and the DMA control register.

name: start_final_code_region
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a raw code region of 238 instructions that calls the system library routines to open and close a library and calls three library offsets, and touches the audio volume registers, the fire button port, a colour register, the DMA control register and the vertical position register.

name: start_intro_code_region
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a raw code region of 342 instructions that calls the system library routines, including a forbid call, touches the third audio channel registers, blitter registers, the keyboard serial register, the fire button port and the DMA control register.

name: start_score_code_region
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a raw code region of 191 instructions that touches the four audio volume registers, the fire button port, the DMA control register and the vertical position register.

name: start_volley_code_region
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so the body is unknown. The facts show a raw code region of 1,374 instructions that calls the forbid and supervisor-state library routines and touches the blitter registers, the third audio channel registers, the keyboard serial register, the fire button port, the DMA control register and the vertical position register.

name: select_language_variant_patches
description: Stores its argument, then chooses one of two base offsets: a zero argument writes return and jump encodings at one set of fixed offsets, while any other argument calls through a stored pointer or writes patches at a second set. The facts show the text references BOOT, ENGLISH and GERMAN, and four unnamed callees.

name: compare_string_against_global
description: Compares a zero-terminated string with bytes at a fixed global address and returns zero when the string ends with every byte matching, or one at the first mismatch. The facts list two unnamed callers and five unnamed callees, though the pseudo-code shows no call.

name: dispatch_rotated_byte_match
description: Rotates a byte left by one bit and, when the result equals a global byte or a fixed constant, calls through a stored pointer. The facts show a version string in the text and three unnamed callers.

name: call_indirect_when_nonzero
description: Calls one routine through a stored pointer and, when the value it leaves in a data register is nonzero, calls a second routine through another stored pointer and returns its result. Three unnamed routines call it, and it calls one unnamed routine.

name: return_register_after_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns the 32-bit value in a data register unchanged. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_argument_and_call_pointer
description: Stores its address argument in one global and the result of a pointer call in another, then returns the two data registers unchanged. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: check_save_file_result
description: Calls a routine through a stored pointer and, when the result equals a fixed constant, calls another unnamed routine, then returns a 32-bit value from a small stack buffer. The facts show the text Xenomorph.save and one unnamed caller.

name: forward_pointer_call_pair
description: Calls one routine through a stored pointer and returns the two data registers unchanged. The facts show the text Xenomorph.save and one unnamed caller.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns. The facts show it was executed in the reference run and entered from outside the static code flow.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with the address taken by a pc-relative load. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: copy_table_then_run_loop
description: Copies a block of 1,936 bytes from one fixed address to another, sets a global routine pointer, then runs a loop of calls that tests global bits and a flag. The bundle pseudo-code is truncated and the facts count only three instructions, so the rest of the routine is not recoverable.

name: run_flag_driven_state_loop
description: Copies 1,936 bytes to a second address, then runs a loop that calls six unnamed routines and tests bits of a global flag word to choose between states. It references the text strings ENGLISH, FAIL, FINISH, TITLE and TUNE, touches the beam control register, and the decompiler truncated the pseudo-code.

name: find_range_record_index
description: Searches a table of four-word records at a fixed address for the first record whose two value ranges contain two current values, and returns its one-based position, or zero when none matches. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: update_flag_bit_and_notify
description: When a global flag word is zero, it checks the results of two unnamed routines and updates the low bit of the flag, calling another unnamed routine on certain transitions. Otherwise it sets the low bit, and the facts show one unnamed caller and one unnamed callee.

name: check_flagged_record_status
description: If a flag with value four is set in a record, it calls one unnamed routine, then checks a linked record for a flag with value two and calls another routine. It returns minus one when a flag in the first record is set and zero otherwise, and the facts show one unnamed caller.

name: load_record_and_process_strings
description: Loads a record's fields into globals and a memory block, then walks two zero-terminated string lists, calling an unnamed routine for each string. It calls several more routines and clears a status word at the end, and the facts show one unnamed caller.

name: find_matching_list_record
description: Walks a linked list of records, comparing three byte fields with global bytes, and on the first match calls an unnamed routine and returns. It was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: find_record_by_register_bytes
description: Walks a linked list comparing three byte values passed in data registers with fields of each record, and calls an unnamed routine on a match. It was decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns the value on top of the stack without other effect. The facts show one unnamed caller and that it was decoded from an unreached gap.

name: build_record_list_from_source
description: Walks a source list while it is nonzero, calling an unnamed routine and filling a new record from each source entry's bytes, then pushes that record onto a global list. It returns zero, and one unnamed routine calls it.

name: copy_long_block_to_fixed
description: Copies 30 long words from one fixed address to another fixed address, then returns. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: store_clamped_offset_sums
description: Stores the incoming value plus 200 in a global, then stores that global plus 436, clamped to the 16-bit maximum, in the same global. The decompiler marks the tail as bad instruction data, so that tail is unreliable.

name: set_fixed_global_constants
description: Writes several fixed constants into global variables and returns. The facts show one tiny routine that loads a constant into a data register as its only callee.

name: allocate_block_from_free_list
description: Rounds a requested size up to a multiple of eight and searches a linked list of free blocks for one large enough, splitting off the remainder when a block is larger. If a flag bit in the second argument is set it zeroes the allocated bytes, and it loops forever when no block fits; four unnamed routines call it.

name: clear_downward_memory_block
description: Zeroes a block of words downward from a pointer global, using a size rounded down to a multiple of eight after adding 32, and loops forever if the pointer falls below a fixed limit. The facts show the colour register as touched and one unnamed caller.

name: subtract_offset_from_global
description: Subtracts the incoming value plus 32 from a global variable and returns. The facts list two tiny routines as callees.

name: free_block_into_list
description: Adds the incoming value to a global total, then inserts the block at the given address into a sorted free list and stores its size rounded up to a multiple of eight. Four unnamed routines call it, and the facts list one unnamed callee.

name: sum_free_list_sizes
description: Walks a free-block list from a fixed head and adds up the size fields, returning the total as a 64-bit result. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: count_prefix_matching_record
description: Walks a linked list of records, and when the input string is a prefix of a record's string it increments that record's counter and returns. If no record matches and a flag word is zero, it calls two unnamed routines, the second only when the first returns nonzero.

name: set_status_bits_and_call
description: Sets bit patterns in two memory bytes, one at an argument pointer and one at a computed offset, then calls three unnamed routines and returns. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: bracket_call_with_status_flag
description: Sets a status word to all ones, calls one unnamed routine, then clears it. If the call returned nonzero it calls two more routines and restores another word, and the facts list one tiny routine as a callee.

name: insert_node_at_list_head
description: Inserts a node at the head of a doubly linked list by clearing its back-link, pointing its forward link at the old head, and updating the old head's back-link when one exists. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: remove_node_from_list
description: Unlinks a node from a doubly linked list by joining its neighbours, or updates the list head when the node has no predecessor. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: carve_typed_entries_into_list
description: Walks a block of entries from a start address, and for each entry whose type field is zero, one or two it links the entry into a global list and computes the next entry's address from its size fields. It stops at any other type or at the end of the block, and the facts show one unnamed callee.

name: find_record_in_hash_bucket
description: Looks up the bucket selected by the high byte of a 16-bit key in a fixed table, and walks its chain of records, stopping at the first record whose key word matches. It returns no value, and two unnamed routines call it.

name: create_record_and_poll
description: Calls an unnamed routine, sets a new record's fields from a global word, calls one of two unnamed routines depending on a flag, and repeats a pair of calls while a status call returns nonzero. Two unnamed routines call it, and it calls one unnamed routine.

name: create_record_with_offset
description: Decoded from an unreached gap, so it may be data. It compares two bytes and moves a record pointer by a fixed offset when they differ, then fills a new record, calls unnamed routines and repeats one call while it returns nonzero.

name: rebuild_hash_buckets
description: Clears a table of 256 bucket pointers, then links each record of a global list into the bucket chosen by its byte field. It returns the incoming value, and the facts show it was executed in the reference run.

name: swap_fields_for_type_two
description: Walks a global list and, for each record whose type field is two, swaps two of its 32-bit fields, then returns the incoming value. The facts list one unnamed callee, though the pseudo-code shows none, and the routine was decoded from an unreached gap.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Only a return, so it returns the value on top of the stack. One unnamed routine calls it, and it was decoded from an unreached gap.

name: bracket_call_with_status_word
description: Sets a status word to all ones, calls one unnamed routine, then clears the word. If the call returned nonzero it calls two more unnamed routines, and the facts show it was executed in the reference run.

name: dispatch_record_state_machine
description: Dispatches on a state field of a record: state zero calls three unnamed routines, state one walks a chain of records calling routines until it reaches a state-two record, and state two stores three values in fixed words and calls another routine. The facts show six unnamed callees and one small routine that loads zero.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Only a return, decoded from an unreached gap. The facts show one unnamed caller and two unnamed callees, though the pseudo-code shows none.
